correctness.rationale: Exact definitions and all quantifiers are given. Replayed standalone source enumerates 24 perfect matchings and both complexes, proves the perfect discrete-Morse matching acyclic across all 8736 directed incidences, computes complete ordinary mod-2 boundaries and rational ranks by exact dimension bounds, enumerates all 336 automorphisms and verifies two independent fixed-simplex/edge-orbit trace formulas for every element, including all swap signs. Verified character equality plus Maschke yields the rational module isomorphism; exact character averages give invariants; rational quotient homology follows via finite-group transfer. Finite enumeration is exhaustive rather than sampling. No integral-module conclusion is claimed.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the full rational sign-twist character identity comparing perfect and ordinary matching complexes, not the previously established perfect homotopy type nor the ordinary homology representation. Relevant original mathematical documents and the two most directly related mathematical records were inspected and compared by logical implication. Neither known result supplies the missing perfect-complex action; exact exhaustive traces were newly verified. Indexed search absence alone was not treated as uniqueness proof.
residual_risks: An equivalent result may be present in unindexed/specialized incidence-geometry literature despite the targeted queries.
The result is an isomorphism class of rational modules; a canonical or integral intertwiner has not been constructed.

value.rationale: For a natural maximal-symmetry incidence graph, the result compares two related but distinct sixteen-dimensional topological representations. Its nontrivial duality sign changes the invariant dimension from one to zero despite matching dimensions, yielding a new rational symmetry-quotient consequence. The graph and invariant are independently motivated by the known perfect-complex homotopy type and known ordinary-complex action; this is not a cosmetic parameter change or a known table recomputation.
